title: Quality-plane regression without runtime continuity loss
summary: Use this pattern when a soak or runtime milestone remains valid, but live release readiness drops because quality gates regress while runtime continuity stays preserved.
detection_signals: runtime continuity remains preserved or stable
daemon remains running and ticks continue advancing
quality gate drops from pass or ready to candidate, degraded, or attention
verification pending checks reappear with quality-related reasons
artifact audit and required artifact presence remain intact

root_cause_buckets.meaning: The underlying model or system capability actually regressed.
The evaluator, rubric, or sample changed enough to flip the verdict without a real capability loss.
A provider, model, or routing profile changed and reduced quality on one capability slice.
Live health is pulled down by stale or misclassified task states such as active-but-queued.

triage_steps: Verify the milestone ledger still shows the historical milestone as committed.
Check runtime continuity and daemon freshness before classifying any regression.
Identify the exact failing quality signal or test case that triggered the live downgrade.
Separate release-readiness regression from self-model or queue-health regression.
Decide whether the failing quality signal belongs to capability_regression, eval_drift, or routing_regression.
Decide whether task state semantics need cleanup to remove false active or stalled pressure.
reporting_rules: Always report milestone validity separately from current live health.
Do not describe the incident as a runtime failure unless continuity evidence broke.
State the single triggering quality signal when available.
List self-model or task-health drag factors as concurrent contributors, not as the primary trigger unless they caused the first downgrade.

report_template.live_health_line: Current live readiness has degraded because quality gate signal(s) regressed.
